title: Enterprise contract decision framework for MSA/DPA: escrow and liability tiers
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem: Enterprise sales are delayed by inconsistent redline decisions across Legal, Sales, and Finance. Current practice: ad-hoc negotiation, multiple points of escalation, and inconsistent liability/indemnity concessions. This results in longer sales cycles, uneven risk posture, and manual rework for Legal on repeat asks.

Goal: Create a repeatable decision framework and triage workflow for MSA/DPA redlines that: 1) standardizes liability and indemnity thresholds by customer tier and revenue; 2) codifies an escrow/escrow-equivalent approach for certain data or model IP requests; 3) defines clear routing and SLAs for Legal, Product, and Security reviews; and 4) produces a short decision log and templates enabling the Sales team to close faster while preserving acceptable risk.

Scope: Focus on common redline buckets observed in Q4 sales (liability caps, carve-outs, indemnity, data handling and escrow requests, security questionnaire deviations). Do not include Pricing discount playbooks (handled by RevOps) except where tied directly to concession thresholds that change risk.
acceptance_criteria: A concise decision matrix mapping customer ARR tiers to allowable liability caps and indemnity language
Escrow decision guidance document with three standardized options (no escrow, vendor-held escrow, neutral escrow agent) and when each applies
Routing playbook: triage steps and SLA (48 hours initial triage, 5 business days for full Legal decision) documented and uploaded to Confluence
Two reusable redline template clauses (liability cap & indemnity) approved by Legal and Product
Pilot run with 4 live enterprise deals showing average time-to-sign decrease vs baseline (target: 18% faster)
proposed_workflow:
1) Sales attaches proposed contract and redline summary to intake form (Confluence template). 2) Triage lead (Sales Ops) classifies request by redline bucket and customer ARR tier. 3) For low-risk standard asks, apply templated clause and close without Legal. 4) For elevated asks (escrow, unlimited liability, broad indemnity), route to Legal + Security + Product with evidence packet (SaaS data map, PII exposure assessment). 5) Legal documents decision in short decision log entry and selects one of three approved dispositions; Finance approves any monetary concessions > X% of ARR. 6) If blocked or novel, escalate to Legal Director + Head of Product for exception approval. 7) Capture final clause and add to contract repository with metadata for future ML-based triage.

SLA targets: 48h initial triage; 5 business days for standard Legal decision; 10 business days for complex/escrow negotiations. Escalation triggers: requests for escrow or indemnity outside approved tiers, requests for on-prem/on-prem data transfer, or novel IP escrow asks.

risks: Risk: Overly permissive templates may expose Redwood to outsized liability — mitigation: strict ARR-tier gating and Finance signoff for higher concessions.
Risk: Sales bypassing playbook for speed — mitigation: require intake form and template insertion into CRM for auditing and quota compensation alignment.
Risk: Novel escrow asks (model weights/IP) create long technical cycles — mitigation: Product-led feasibility checklist and a ‘manual review’ bucket with longer SLA.
